snackbar-provider.purpose: Coordinate transient feedback queues, placement, timing, undo, retry, and live-region behavior for non-blocking product events.
useWhen: Multiple actions or system events can emit toasts/snackbars.
Feedback needs queueing, placement, deduplication, undo, or retry policy.
The app shell needs one consistent feedback region.
doNotUseWithoutReview: A single local Toast is enough.
The message asks for a required decision.
Duration, queue behavior, severity, or undo policy is unclear.
foundations: Defines feedback region placement, safe area, stack spacing, and viewport behavior.
Owns concise event copy, undo/retry labels, and severity language.
Controls tone, priority, dismiss, action, and stacked emphasis.
Queued, visible, actioned, dismissed, retrying, failed, and empty states are explicit.
Feedback floats above content without blocking required actions.
Live region role, announcement priority, keyboard actions, and focus behavior are required.
slots: Shared feedback area owned by the shell or route.
Undo, retry, view, or dismiss actions.
Duration, dedupe, max visible count, and priority rules.
variants: Multiple non-blocking confirmations share one region.
Undo action is available only when product behavior exists.
Recoverable system event exposes retry without blocking the page.
motion: Items appear in the region with reduced-motion fallback.
Dismiss removes one item without moving focus unexpectedly.
Stacking preserves safe-area and primary action access.
accessibility: Feedback uses the right live-region priority.
Dismiss and undo behavior are real.
The region does not cover required navigation or primary actions.
tests: Queue shows newest feedback in region.
Undo/retry action produces a visible result.
Stack does not cover primary actions.

canDecide: Use Snackbar Provider when a route or shell owns multiple transient feedback events.
Use Toast as the visible item.
Limit actions to real undo, retry, or view behavior.
mustAsk: Duration, max stack, undo policy, retry behavior, or severity priority is unclear.
Feedback affects finance, compliance, legal, security, or identity state.
rejectIf: The feedback asks for a blocking decision.
Queue and live-region behavior are undefined.
miel.handoff: Confirm placement, queue limits, duration, live-region role, severity priority, undo/retry behavior, and dismiss policy.
